thesis.title: COIN — HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY candidate (Q3 2024 SEC disclosure screen pass)
thesis.thesis: HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY CANDIDATE ONLY — not an investment conclusion. Coinbase Global, Inc. (COIN) passed a single frozen, offline, SEC-disclosure-only screen rule: issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY growth >= 20%. Per the Q3 2024 shareholder letter (period Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, released 2024-10-30), total revenue was $1,205,193 thousand versus $674,148 thousand in Q3 2023, a derived YoY rate of 78.8% (derived from the two reported figures; the adapter labels it "derived"). This establishes only that the one top-line growth rule was met on that historical period. It says nothing about share price, valuation, analyst targets, future returns, or current market data — all of which were explicitly excluded dimensions of the screen. Passing this rule does not mean COIN is an attractive investment, and this single-issuer historical result must not be ranked against other issuers or treated as contemporaneous.
assumptions: The 78.8% YoY figure is a derived calculation from two issuer-reported total revenue values ($1,205,193k Q3 2024 vs $674,148k Q3 2023), not a directly stated growth rate; it is only valid under the issuer's own total_revenue label and matched prior-year period.
The screen's basis warning notes issuer top-line labels differ (total revenue vs total net revenues); COIN's label here is total_revenue, so no cross-issuer comparison of these rates is valid.
The screen is a frozen offline SEC-source adapter, not live market data; the packet's as_of timestamp is the adapter run time, not a market date.
No price, valuation, or market-cap input exists in this packet, so no valuation-based conclusion can be drawn.
catalysts: Future issuer SEC disclosures (subsequent quarterly shareholder letters / 10-Qs) that would show whether the Q3 2024 revenue level and mix persisted or reversed.
Disclosure of transaction-revenue trend recovery or further contraction in later periods.
invalidations: A later issuer-reported period showing top-line revenue YoY growth below 20% under the same label and matched prior-year basis would break the only rule this candidate passed.
Evidence that the 78.8% derived rate rests on a mismatched period or a label change (e.g., total revenue redefined) would invalidate the screen pass itself.
Evidence that the QoQ revenue contraction was driven by a structural, not cyclical, decline in transaction revenue would undercut the growth premise.

message.content:
# COIN — Historical SEC-Disclosure Candidate Research

**Scope note:** This is a historical, SEC-disclosure-only exercise using a frozen offline source adapter (fixture `FINTECH-SEC-SCREEN-HOLDOUT-v1`). It is not live market data, not a contemporaneous peer ranking, and not an investment recommendation. No trades were placed and no live market tools were used.

## 1. Screen outcome — RETAINED (1 of 1)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Symbol / company | COIN — Coinbase Global, Inc. |
| Reporting period | Q3 2024, ended 2024-09-30 |
| Release date | 2024-10-30 |
| Source | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978824000186/q324shareholderletter.htm` |
| Full SHA-256 | `f9a2d60153fd79c6ac9f7dfcd80344995ffa4b121c336808b2e2f13968230a52` |
| Locators | Q3 2024 shareholder letter p.3 operating summary; Q3 2024 condensed consolidated statements of operations |
| Rule applied | `reported_top_line_revenue_yoy_min_percent >= 20.0` |
| Reported top-line label | `total_revenue` |
| Total revenue Q3 2024 | $1,205,193 thousand |
| Total revenue Q3 2023 | $674,148 thousand |
| YoY growth | 78.8% — **derived** from the two reported values, not directly stated |
| Failed criteria | None |
| Fact IDs | COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2024, COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2023, COIN-Q3-REV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-TRANREV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-NETINCOME, COIN-Q3-CRYPTOLOSS |

**Metric basis and units:** issuer-reported `total_revenue` in USD thousands, as presented in the shareholder letter. The adapter's basis warning notes issuer top-line labels differ (total revenue vs. total net revenues); COIN's label here is `total_revenue`, so this rate is valid only under COIN's own label and matched prior-year period and must not be compared across issuers.

**Excluded dimensions (per the adapter):** share price, valuation, analyst target, future return, current market data. None were supplied or used.

## 2. Independent counterpoint (different supplied field)

The most material counterpoint is **not** the YoY pass but the sequential trend in the same disclosure: **total revenue fell 17% quarter-over-quarter** (`total_revenue_qoq_percent_reported` = −17), and **transaction revenue fell 27% QoQ** (`transaction_revenue_qoq_percent_reported` = −27). The 78.8% YoY rate is measured against a depressed Q3 2023 base, so it coexists with a sharp sequential contraction concentrated in the most cyclical revenue line. A growth screen that reads only the YoY field would miss this.

A secondary, also-different field: a **$121M rounded pretax crypto investment portfolio loss** was reported alongside **$75M rounded net income** — i.e., reported profitability was materially affected by mark-to-market swings on the crypto investment portfolio. Both are rounded figures as supplied.

## 3. Thesis saved (exactly one, historical preliminary)

- **Thesis ID:** `th_f7e10af704924dc2b865` — status `researching`, conviction 2/5, version 1.
- Structured evidence includes the full source URL, full SHA-256, release date, period, units, metric basis, fact IDs, locators, the counterpoint, and an explicit missing-data boundary.
- `next_review_at` was **omitted** (no genuinely future-dated review was warranted).

**Discriminating follow-up question:** In the next issuer-reported period, did total revenue and transaction revenue stabilize or continue contracting sequentially — and if YoY growth stayed above 20%, was that driven by a still-depressed prior-year base rather than by sequential recovery in transaction revenue?

**Missing price/valuation boundary:** No share price, market capitalization, valuation multiple, or analyst target was supplied. This thesis makes no valuation conclusion and no claim about whether the historical growth rate was reflected in price.

## 4. Explicit limits

- Passing this single top-line rule does **not** mean COIN was or is an attractive investment; it is one historical disclosure test, not a seven-factor completeness screen.
- This is a single-issuer historical result and must not be ranked against other issuers or treated as contemporaneous.
- Absences in this packet are packet omissions, not SEC filing omissions — the adapter supplied a subset of fields, and nothing here should be read as a statement that the issuer failed to disclose anything.
